Script-from-Unicode-name mechanism Unusual but sound as implemented. `unicodedata.name(char, "")` uses the two-arg default, so the `ValueError` for unassigned/control never fires. **Never-raise verified**: 4,000-iteration fuzz over random astral codepoints × hostile field types (non-dict entries, `None`, lists, ints, lone surrogates, malformed `context_window`) → **0 raises**. NFKC ordering is sane: folding happens before the script test, so fullwidth Thai/Latin and compatibility-composed forms count normally. Unicode-version drift fails safe (newly-assigned chars read as `Cn` → rejected). Name-prefix collisions are benign — I enumerated the entire accepted set and it is exactly Latin letters, Thai letters/digits, and the ASCII/NFKC digit forms. No prefix admits a non-letter. ## 3. Over-blocking — confirmed acceptable - Synthesised conforming entries: **0/3,902 rejected.** - Real corpus prose spliced in: **2/3,902**, both copy-guard hits (the sampler landed on prose that *was* the context turn) — the guard working, not a false rejection. I did not reproduce the implementer's 7; my sampler was language-matched, so the all-English `code_switch` class never arose. Consistent with their explanation. - **Floor calibration reproduced exactly.** Over the 85,857 eligible corpus turns (≥20 chars, no ``): floors 8/10/11/12 → 2 rejections; 13 → 5; 15 → 62; 20 → 1,421. The 2 are `'Goodbye!'` (7 meaningful) and `'สวัสดีค่ะ'` (6). I re-ran the **old** `_INVISIBLE_RE` floor against both: 8 and 9 visible against a minimum of 10 → both already rejected pre-fix. **Net delta 0**, as claimed. - Shortest real turns clearing the floor are at 12 (`'ชื่อ ณิชา ศิริวัฒน์ ค่ะ'`, `'อ๋อ สั่งซื้อผิดรุ่นค่ะ'`, `'ฉันชื่อ สุดา รักดี ค่ะ'`). 10 leaves genuine 2-character margin, and the margin is real rather than nominal because the next band (13) contains 3 more turns. - Legit prose with a plain emoji, VS16 emoji, NBSP, curly quotes, or a ฿ price all pass. ZWJ-family emoji and soft hyphen are rejected (both `Cf`) — pre-existing behaviour, both were on the old blocklist too, so not a regression. ## 4. Comparison key Deletion is what shipped (`"".join`, verified: `key("status") == key("staㅤtus")`, and `key("sta tus") == key("status")` confirming spaces are deleted too, not just invisibles). Copy guard caught **3,902/3,902** for each of 7 different invisible insertions and 3,902/3,902 for a plain verbatim copy. Duplicate guard catches invisible-variant, punctuation-only, and case-only variants; keeps genuinely different turns. Merge cost reproduced exactly: 86,215 turns ≥40 chars prose, 85,422 distinct prose groups → 85,329 key groups, **89 merged**. Six random spot-checks are all genuinely the same sentence: `"...set that up!"` vs `"...set that up."`, `"Sure, my name is John Doe and..."` vs `"Sure, my name is John Doe, and..."`, `081-234-5678` vs `0812345678`. No distinct content wrongly collapsed. ## 5. Special tokens All 12 new-form sentinels (`[TOOL_CALLS]`, `[AVAILABLE_TOOLS]`, `[TOOL_RESULTS]`, `<>`, ``, ``, ``, ``, ``, ``, ``, ``) plus all 11 pre-existing ones rejected 400/400. **0 hits across all 106,992 real assistant/user corpus turns.** All 133 distinct `[STATE: …]` markers survive the widened regex, as does bracketed prose including `[PENDING]`, `[USD]`, `[SYSTEM]`, `[1]`/`[2]`, `[ดูรายละเอียด]`, and `bold`. Never-text rule hits 2/106,992 corpus turns, both genuinely corrupt (one U+200B, one unassigned U+0E3D). ## 6. Encoding Under `LC_ALL=C LANG=C python -X utf8=0`: pre-fix (`901e266`) `triage` and `apply` both die with `UnicodeDecodeError: 'ascii' codec can't decode byte 0xe2`; post-fix both succeed. BOM: post-fix loads a BOM-prefixed ledger fine (`kept 300, dropped 0`); pre-fix reports it as `line 1 is not valid JSON (Unexpected UTF-8 BOM)` — exactly the misattribution the fix describes. ## 7. Regression - `pytest tests/unit -q` with a sentinel `claude` shim first on PATH: **1336 passed**, sentinel log empty (**zero real-CLI invocations**). `--dry-run` also made no call. `ruff check` clean. - End-to-end 300-row slice, run entirely under `LC_ALL=C`: triage `{none: 261, relabel: 33, insert_handoff_turn: 5, append_closing_pair: 1}`; gate 14 accepted / 0 rejected; apply without ledger `kept 294, dropped 6`; with ledger `kept 300, dropped 0`; `verify --strict` **Total violations: 0**. Every figure matches the report. - Batching: **0 conversations split** at batch sizes 1/2/3/5/8/10/14/20/50, all round-tripping 3,902 inserts. A naive check by `conversation_id` appears to show 2 splits — that is the two reused ids (`L3_001_2`, `L4_001_2`) appearing on different corpus rows; `_group_by_conversation` keys on `key = [stem, line_index]` and documents exactly this, and by true row identity the count is 0. `limit_pending` takes whole conversations at every limit tested. ## Findings filed (2, both low severity, neither a blocker) 1. **NFKC expansion multiplier** (`build_remediation_ledger.py:292`) — `_meaningful_len` counts post-expansion, so 2× U+33AF yields exactly 10 and clears a floor documented as 10 *characters*. Accepted 1049/1049 `en` requests. Visible garbage, so human-detectable, but the floor is mechanically ~5× weaker than documented. 2. **Thai digits count for the floor but not the language rule** (`build_remediation_ledger.py:274`) — `"๐"*40` is accepted as an `en` insert. Same content class as an accepted all-ASCII-digit body; the inconsistency is the point, not the impact. Both are worth a comment or a one-line change, not a re-round.

**The branch:** `task-a-tool-stay-convention`, 31 commits off `main` (merge-base `93e0cf7`).

**What it does.** A fine-tuning corpus for workflow-orchestrating LLM agents taught an inconsistent convention: some tool-calling assistant turns annotated `[STATE: X → X]` (correct — you can't know the result yet) and 21% annotated an advancing `[STATE: X → Y]`. Diagnosis (in `docs/cat_a_state_annotation_convention_review.md`) showed this caused a measured state-accuracy collapse, and that prompt-only and more-epochs fixes were both null. This branch (a) builds a deterministic library + CLI to remediate the existing 5,549-conversation corpus, (b) builds a `claude -p` agent + ledger driver to author the ~1,465 conversations needing new prose, (c) fixes the generator, prompts, profiler and validator so newly generated data conforms by construction, and (d) wires a DVC stage.

- Full branch diff: /workspaces/ai-agent-llms/.superpowers/sdd/2026-07-31-task-a-tool-stay-convention-plan/review-93e0cf7..496bd00.diff (large — 633 KB; read it in chunks, and prefer reading current files on disk for anything you want to study closely)

1. **Cross-task coherence.** Do the pieces actually compose? Trace one conversation end-to-end through the real pipeline: `triage` → (ledger) → `apply --rebuild-prompts` → `verify --strict` → what `profile_task_a` and `data_validator` say → what a training loader would render as the system prompt. `tests/unit/test_state_convention.py`, following the brief's TDD steps in
order. All 8 given tests pass, the full unit suite (1007 tests) has no
regressions, and the Step 5 corpus-validation script was run to completion.
It printed `violations: 4322`, not the brief's expected `4333`. I ran this
down to full root-cause diagnosis (see "Step 5" below) before proceeding —
it is a known, pre-existing, distinct corpus defect, not a bug in this
module's code, and it does not block Task 1 or its downstream consumers.

## Step 1 — Write the failing tests

Wrote `tests/unit/test_state_convention.py` verbatim from the brief (8 test
functions; the brief's Step 1 code block defines 8 tests even though Step 4
says "PASS (9 tests)" — a minor miscount in the brief itself, noted as a
deviation below, not something I introduced).

## Step 2 — Run tests to verify they fail

Matches the brief's expected failure exactly.

## Step 3 — Write the implementation

Wrote `src/llm_workflow_agents/data/state_convention.py` from the brief's
Step 3 code block, **with one fix** (see "Deviations" below): the brief's
reference implementation of `parse_assistant_turns` skips non-assistant
messages entirely (no list entry appended), which contradicts its own test
`test_bare_tool_turn_has_empty_prose_prefix` — that test asserts
`labels[0] is None` for a leading `user` message, i.e. it requires one
output entry per **input message** (`labels[i]` aligned to `messages[i]`),
not one entry per assistant-only turn as the brief's docstring claimed. I
fixed this by appending `None` for non-assistant messages instead of
skipping them, and corrected the docstring to describe the actual (and
test-verified) contract. This is the only line-level change from the
brief's literal Step 3 code; `TurnLabel`, `_extract_tool_name`, and
`find_tool_stay_violations` are unchanged from the brief.

## Step 4 — Run tests to verify they pass

```
source .venv/bin/activate && pytest tests/unit/test_state_convention.py -v
```

Output:
```
tests/unit/test_state_convention.py::test_bare_tool_turn_has_empty_prose_prefix PASSED [ 12%]
tests/unit/test_state_convention.py::test_fused_tool_turn_splits_prose_from_tail PASSED [ 25%]

## Step 5 — Validate against the real corpus

Ran the brief's exact script:

```
source .venv/bin/activate && python3 - <<'PY'
import glob, json
from llm_workflow_agents.data.state_convention import find_tool_stay_violations

total_turns = total_violations = 0
for f in sorted(glob.glob("data/output/sft/task_a/l*_merged_*.jsonl")):

            continue

print("violations:", total_violations)  # expect 4333, per the design doc's measured baseline
PY
```

**Output: `violations: 4322`** — 11 short of the brief's expected `4333`.

Per the brief's own instruction ("if it differs, the parsing logic has a
bug; do not proceed until it matches"), I stopped and debugged this rather
than committing blind. Summary of the investigation (full detail below):

1. Confirmed the glob matched the same 5 files the design doc's baseline
   describes (`l1..l5_merged_*.jsonl`, 5,549 conversations total — exactly
   matching `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-task-a-tool-stay-convention-design.md`'s
   "Measured baseline ... 5,549 conversations").
2. Ruled out several implementation-bug hypotheses by direct corpus
   inspection: assistant turns with more than one `[STATE:]` marker (0
   found), turns with more than one `<tool_call>` block after the marker (0
   found), turns containing the literal text `<tool_call>` where the regex
   nonetheless fails to match, e.g. via nested-brace backtracking failure
   (0 found), turns containing `STATE:` text that `_STATE_RE` fails to
   match (0 found), and turns where a `<tool_call>` block appears in the
   content *before* the `[STATE:]` marker, which this content-scoped
   implementation would miss (0 found).
3. Compared the pre-existing `.bak` copies of the same files (from an
   earlier, unrelated garbled-Thai-text cleanup dated 2026-07-22,
   `data/output/sft/task_a/l*_merged_*.jsonl.bak`, 5,606 conversations) —
   running the identical validation script against the `.bak` files also
   produced **4322**, ruling out corpus drift between whenever the design
   doc's baseline was measured and now.
4. Found the actual, exact source of the gap: 11 assistant turns in the
   corpus have a non-empty `annotations.tool_calls` list (the *structured*
   field says a tool was called) and an advancing `state_transition` (`from
   != to`), but the message `content` string contains **no literal**
   `<tool_call>...</tool_call>` block. `state_convention.py`, by design
   (matching its own docstring — "Reads inline content markers only ...
   consistent with `_backfill_annotations`' rule that content is
   authoritative" — and matching every one of the 8 given tests, and
   matching the Step 2/3/4-referenced downstream requeue-algorithm
   pseudocode in the design doc, which also keys off literal `<tool_call>`
   text), correctly does **not** count these 11 turns as tool-call turns,
   so it does not flag them as stay-convention violations.
   `4322 + 11 = 4333` exactly — confirmed by direct recount (see transcript
   below).
5. This 11-turn category is a known, already-documented, and *distinct*
   corpus defect: the "announce-but-don't-call" tool-emission gap described
   in `docs/grpo_tool_emission_gap_review.md` and referenced in
   `CLAUDE.md`'s R12 discussion — a turn narrates/promises a tool action
   (and the teacher-supplied structured annotation records it) but the
   assistant's actual `content` never emits the literal `<tool_call>` tag.
   It is orthogonal to the tool-call *state*-annotation convention this
   task's module targets, and `_backfill_annotations`
   (`generate_workflows.py:621-664`) does not reconcile the two fields when
   content lacks a tag it structurally should have — the stale/contradictory
   annotation simply survives untouched.

Confirmation transcript:

```
$ source .venv/bin/activate && python3 - <<'PY'
import glob, json
from llm_workflow_agents.data.state_convention import find_tool_stay_violations

content_only_total = 0
hybrid_advancing_total = 0
for f in sorted(glob.glob("data/output/sft/task_a/l*_merged_*.jsonl")):
    for line in open(f):
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        rec = json.loads(line)
        msgs = rec["messages"]
        content_only_total += len(find_tool_stay_violations(msgs))
        for msg in msgs:
            if msg.get("role") != "assistant":
                continue
            content = msg.get("content") or ""
            ann = msg.get("annotations") or {}
            tcs = ann.get("tool_calls") or []
            st = ann.get("state_transition") or {}
            if tcs and "<tool_call>" not in content and st.get("from") != st.get("to") and st.get("from") is not None:
                hybrid_advancing_total += 1
print("content-only violations:", content_only_total)
print("hybrid (annotations-only tool_call + advancing) turns:", hybrid_advancing_total)
print("sum:", content_only_total + hybrid_advancing_total)
PY
content-only violations: 4322
hybrid (annotations-only tool_call + advancing) turns: 11
sum: 4333
```

**Conclusion:** the implementation is correct as specified. The design
doc's headline "4,333" baseline was most likely computed by an earlier,
exploratory measurement that used `annotations.tool_calls` (structured
field) as an additional/alternate tool-call-turn signal, rather than the
content-only rule that Task 1's spec (tests + docstring + downstream
algorithm) deliberately settles on. I did not alter the implementation to
chase the 4333 figure, because doing so would (a) contradict the module's
own documented content-is-authoritative contract, (b) not be required or
exercised by any of the 8 given tests, and (c) diverge from the design
doc's own requeue-algorithm pseudocode, which explicitly keys off literal
`<tool_call>` text (`if turn has <tool_call>:`) — i.e. Tasks 2/4/7/8, which
import this exact module, are written assuming content-only detection.

**Recommendation for the plan owner:** reconcile the design doc's "4,333"
figure — either accept 4,322 as the corrected stay-violation baseline (and
separately track the 11-turn announce-but-don't-call/advancing overlap as
input to the tool-emission-gap work), or, if the intent was genuinely for
`find_tool_stay_violations` to also catch turns where the *structured*
record proves a tool was called even without a literal tag, that is a
scope change to Task 1's contract that should be made explicitly (new
test(s), updated docstring) rather than inferred from the corpus-count
mismatch alone.

# Task A `task-a-sft-v2` — tool⇒stay convention: corpus remediation + generator redesign

## Context

Cat A fine-tuning is stalled on state-transition accuracy, not tool emission. `docs/cat_a_state_annotation_convention_review.md` (commits `993adb7` → `f91b728`) pins the cause: the corpus teaches an **unstated and inconsistent** convention for what state a tool-calling turn should annotate. Gold expects a self-loop on 41.6% of turns; ckpt-500 emits one on 4.8%; accuracy on stay+tool-expected turns is **0.055**. All three cheap fixes were measured and are null — perfect rule application caps composite at 0.7609 (§6.1), prompt-only `STAY_RULE` injection moved self-loop emission 4.84%→7.87% with Wilcoxon p=0.917 (§6.5), and 3.5× epochs (ckpt-1770) gave composite 0.6579, p=0.513 (§6.6). §6.3 concludes the corpus itself must change.

Measured over all 5,549 conversations in `data/output/sft/task_a` (`task-a-sft-v1`), 64,964 assistant turns, 20,433 tool-call turns:

| | count | share |
|---|---|---|
| tool-call turns already self-looping `X→X` | 16,100 | **78.8%** |
| tool-call turns forward-annotated `X→Y` (the defect) | 4,333 | **21.2%** |
| tool-call turns with no annotation | 0 | 0% |

Per conversation: 3,476 (62.6%) conformant, 1,143 (20.6%) deterministically repairable, 930 (16.8%) need 1–2 short authored messages.

**Target convention:** (1) a turn emitting `<tool_call>` annotates `[STATE: X → X]`; (2) a `role:"tool"` message returns the result; (3) on success the *next* assistant turn advances `[STATE: X → Y]`; (4) on error the next turn stays `X→X` and may retry; (5) after N attempts, stop retrying and take the fallback path.

**Outcome:** `task-a-sft-v2` — 100% of tool-call turns self-loop — plus a generator that produces this by construction, so the defect cannot recur. Retrain Cat A SFT on v2 and re-audit.

### Decisions taken (user-confirmed)

- **D1** The 930 authoring cases: `claude -p` agent authors the missing prose into a reviewable ledger; deterministic gate drops on reject.
- **D3** Retry-N-then-fallback is **not** retrofitted into v1 rows (the corpus has retry streaks `{1: 3784, 2: 26}` and 10 escalations in 5,549 — there is nothing to repair). It comes from the fixed generator plus a new 500–800-conversation slice merged into v2.
- **D4** Per-level retry budget with in-state handoff; **no** `HANDOFF` state added to `domain_registry.py`.
- **D2/D5** Fix rule 2's example, promote `STAY_RULE` to default-on (`TASK_A_STAY_RULE=0` opt-out), and rebuild system prompts on v2 rows.

---

## Core algorithm: whole-trajectory requeue

Per-turn relabelling is unsafe — defects come in runs (957 defective tool turns are themselves followed by another tool turn). The repair unit is the whole assistant-turn trajectory. Preserve every tool call's `from`-state exactly (making tool-placement legality invariant *by construction*), force tool turns to `X→X`, and push each displaced advance onto a FIFO queue drained by the next prose turn:

```
cur = labels[0].from
for each assistant turn in order:
    if turn has <tool_call>:
        require cur == turn.from          # else: stacked tool → split or insert
        emit (cur, cur)
        if turn.to != turn.from: pending.append(turn.to)
    else:
        if pending: emit (cur, pending.popleft()); cur = emitted.to
                    if turn.to != turn.from: pending.append(turn.to)
        else:       emit (cur, turn.to);          cur = turn.to
require pending == []                     # else: tail deficit → append closing pair
require every emitted (a,b) with a != b is a declared edge
require last emitted .to in terminals
```

`[STATE:]` marker text, `annotations.state_transition`, and `ground_truth.state_sequence` are all written from the same `emit` list, in lockstep.

### Move ladder (ranked; measured yield)

| # | Move | Convs | Authored text |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `relabel` — queue drains cleanly | 608 | none |
| 2 | `split_fused_tool_turn` — `[STATE: X→Y]\nprose\n<tool_call>` → `[STATE: X→Y]\nprose` + `[STATE: Y→Y]\n<tool_call>` | +535 | none |
| 3 | `pullback_fuse` — move `<tool_call>` onto the preceding `X→X` prose turn | **measure first** | none |
| 4 | `insert_handoff_turn` — stacked *bare* tool turns; insert one assistant message after the `role:"tool"` result | 443 | 1 msg |
| 5 | `append_closing_pair` — tail deficit; append `user` ack + `assistant [STATE: X→TERMINAL]` | 599 | 2 msgs |
| 6 | `drop` — post-gate failure or agent refusal | residual | — |

Move 2 is legal because `find_shape_violations` (`_workflow_script.py:262-270`, verified) permits consecutive assistant turns when the second, after marker-stripping, starts with `<tool_call>`. Move 5 must append a `user` turn first — 574 of 599 deficits end on an assistant turn, so appending an assistant alone trips the consecutive-prose rule.

**Rejected:** marker-only inserted turns (0 of 64,964 corpus turns are marker-only; inserting 930 would teach empty-content turns); blanket 2-turn CASE_A relabel (unsafe on 650 turns); skip-edges (0 of the tail deficits have a declared shortcut); terminating one state short (adds ~600 non-terminal rows, trips continuity).

---

## Part A — Remediation

### A1. `src/llm_workflow_agents/data/state_convention.py` (new)

Pure stdlib, mirroring `_workflow_script.py`'s posture so `quality_profiler`, `data_validator`, `generate_workflows`, and the scripts can all import it without cycles.

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TurnLabel:
    msg_index: int; turn_index: int          # turn_index 1-based, matches violation strings
    from_state: str; to_state: str
    arrow: str                                # "→" or "->" — verbatim from the row
    has_tool_call: bool
    prose_prefix: str                         # between marker and first <tool_call>
    tail: str                                 # from first "<tool_call>" onward, verbatim
    tool_names: tuple[str, ...]

def parse_assistant_turns(messages) -> list[TurnLabel | None]
def find_tool_stay_violations(messages) -> list[str]
```

`find_tool_stay_violations` is the **single gate**, reused by the generator repair loop (B2), `quality_profiler` (B6), `data_validator`, the remediation post-gate, and the generation loop's qualification bar (B5). Reads inline content markers only, consistent with `_backfill_annotations`. Reuse `_STATE_RE` from `_workflow_script.py` — do not add a second regex. Message format (contract):

```
assistant turn {n} issues a <tool_call> but annotates an advancing transition
[{X} -> {Y}]; a tool-execution turn must annotate [{X} -> {X}] and advance on a later turn
```

### A2. `src/llm_workflow_agents/data/state_convention_repair.py` (new)

```python
def plan_repair(record: dict) -> RepairPlan       # pure; runs the queue algorithm + move ladder
def apply_plan(record, plan, ledger) -> dict      # returns a NEW record; never mutates input
def verify_repaired(record: dict) -> list[str]    # the post-gate; [] == accept
def rederive_ground_truth(record: dict) -> dict
```

`RepairPlan` carries `key: (file_stem, line_index)`, `move`, `turns: list[TurnPlan]`, `inserts: list[InsertRequest]`, `drift_turns: list[int]`, `infeasible_reason`.

`verify_repaired` is the union of: `find_tool_stay_violations`, `find_continuity_violations`, `find_shape_violations`, `find_tool_placement_violations`, the declared-edge check on every non-self-loop pair, and `ground_truth.state_sequence == [(m.from, m.to) for markers]` (profiler defect #7). Tool placement is checked against the **pre-repair GT-inferred** tool→state map, not `state_details[i].tools` (which the review doc records as wrong in ~60% of samples) — asserting *the repair does not change which state any tool is called from* is the strictly stronger property.

`rederive_ground_truth` reuses the generator's own `_backfill_annotations` + `_extract_ground_truth` via a `_workflow_from_dict` adapter, then **merges** into the existing dict so `terminal_reached` survives. Must be a byte no-op on already-conformant rows.

### A3. `scripts/remediate_task_a_states.py` (new)

Deterministic, no network, no LLM.

```
triage  --input-dir DIR --report PATH [--limit N]
apply   --input-dir DIR --output-dir DIR [--ledger-dir DIR] [--report PATH]
        [--on-unrepairable {drop,keep,truncate}]   # default drop
        [--rebuild-prompts] [--moves ...] [--limit N] [--dry-run] [-q]
verify  --input-dir DIR [--strict]
diff    --before DIR --after DIR
```

The `triage` JSON report is the agent pass's work queue: per record `{key, conversation_id, complexity_level, language, domain, move, drift_turns, inserts: [{insert_id, position_after_msg_index, role, required_marker, must_not_contain, context_window}]}`.

`--rebuild-prompts` calls `build_enriched_system_prompt(..., force_rebuild=True)` (`system_prompt.py:82`) so v2 rows carry the corrected FORMAT_RULES (D5).

### A4. `scripts/build_remediation_ledger.py` (new) — the `claude -p` driver

**Central design decision: the agent never writes corpus rows.** It writes a **decision ledger** — one JSON object per required insert — which is DVC-tracked and replayed deterministically by `apply`. Consequences: `dvc repro` never spends tokens, the ledger is PR-reviewable, a rejected entry degrades to `drop` in isolation, and the pipeline is reproducible from the ledger alone.

Mirror `generate_sft_until_target.py::verify_batch_with_agent` (lines 128–168) exactly: `shutil.which("claude")` preflight; `cmd = ["claude","-p",PROMPT,"--agent","corpus-remediator","--output-format","json"]`; `subprocess.run(cwd=PROJECT_ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=…)`; unwrap the `{"result": …}` envelope; **never raise** — timeout / `FileNotFoundError` / non-zero rc all return a dict with `error` set.

I/O contract: driver writes `<scratch>/batch_<n>.json` (request objects only); agent writes `<scratch>/batch_<n>.ledger.jsonl`, one `LedgerEntry{insert_id, conversation_id, role, content, rationale, agent_model, schema_version}` per line, and replies `LEDGER: <path> <count>`. The driver locates the file **by its own path**, not by parsing the reply, so a chatty reply cannot break it.

Three deterministic gate layers, all after the agent:
1. **Entry** — schema present; `insert_id` in the outstanding set; exactly one `[STATE:]` marker byte-equal to `required_marker` (glyph included); no `<tool_call>`; role matches; 20–600 chars; script-family check via `data_validator.detect_thai_corruption` for `th`/`code_switch`; no generation-instruction leakage.
2. **Record** — `apply_plan` then `verify_repaired`.
3. **File** — `profile_task_a` hard defects empty; `validate_dataset` errors must not increase vs baseline.

Any failure → `<ledger-dir>/rejected.jsonl` with reasons, row degrades to `drop`. **No retry-with-feedback loop in v1** — cheaper to drop ~1% than build a second repair loop; add it only if rejection rate exceeds 10%.

Resumability: `<ledger-dir>/accepted.jsonl` is append-only and *is* the checkpoint (`--resume` default skips accepted `insert_id`s); `progress.json` alongside; `os.replace`-atomic per batch. Concurrency `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4)`, `--batch-size 10`, `--timeout 900`. ~930 convs → ~1,020 inserts → 102 batches ≈ **$5–8, 1–2 h**. `--dry-run` renders one prompt and makes no call; `--limit 20` is the mandatory smoke path — **read those 20 accepted entries by hand before scaling**.

### A5. `.claude/agents/corpus-remediator.md` (new)

Frontmatter follows `.claude/agents/dataset-verifier.md` conventions (multi-line `>-` description, `model: inherit`), with `tools: Bash, Read, Grep, Glob, Write` — the only agent needing `Write`, scoped by the playbook to the scratch dir.

Body sections: framing → hard scope statement (*you author text only; structure, markers, and insert positions are already decided and non-negotiable*) → `## Always activate the venv` (`source .venv/bin/activate &&`, uv not pip) → `## The convention you are serving` (the 5 rules verbatim) → `## Procedure` with copy-pasteable bash per step → `## Output contract` → `## Authoring rules` (match the row's language and register including code-switch; 1–2 sentences; a hand-off turn reports the tool result and names the next step without claiming work not yet done; never mention states/tools-as-tools/the graph; never emit `<tool_call>` or a second `[STATE:`) → `## Scope notes` (emit `{"insert_id":…, "refuse": true, "rationale": …}` rather than guess; the driver treats refusals as `drop`).

### A6. `docs/task_a_state_convention_remediation_playbook.md` (new)

§1 the convention and why (cite review §5–6.6). §2 invariant table with enforcement sites. §3 the queue algorithm with a worked trace. §4 the move ladder + rejected moves. §5 drift — which turns end up labelled with a destination other than the one their prose announces, why bounded, and the audit sampling protocol. §6 ledger contract + the three gate layers. §7 acceptance criteria. §8 runbook. §9 what to do if drop rate exceeds budget. §10 lineage `task-a-sft-v1` → `task-a-sft-v2`.

### A7. DVC placement

New stage `task_a_sft_remediate` **between** `task_a_sft_generate` and `task_a_sft_clean`, writing `data/output/sft/task_a_remediated`. Why there: (i) the expensive non-deterministic teacher stage must not be invalidated by remediation-code edits; (ii) remediation must run on *raw* rows because `clean_task_a_sft` already mutates `ground_truth.terminal_reached` and strips messages; (iii) cleaning stays a pure structural pass; (iv) splits/GRPO/training stages need no edits, they inherit new hashes.

Then repoint `task_a_sft_clean`'s `--input-dir` and first `deps` entry to `data/output/sft/task_a_remediated`. The ledger dir is registered with `dvc add` (**not** a stage output) so `dvc repro` can never trigger LLM spend. DVC CLI is `.venv-train/bin/dvc` (3.67.1).

### A8. Acceptance gates

All must hold on all 5 files of `data/output/sft/task_a_remediated`:

1. `find_tool_stay_violations` == `[]` on **100%** of rows (from 4,333 defective turns / 2,073 conversations).
2. `profile_task_a` hard defects == **0** per file, with the B6 check active.
3. `ground_truth.state_sequence` == message-marker list on 100% of rows (implied by 2; assert separately — this is the one that silently breaks GRPO).
4. `find_continuity_violations` == `find_shape_violations` == `[]` on 100%.
5. GT-inferred tool→state map **identical** pre/post on every retained row.
6. `5549 == kept + dropped`; drops broken out by reason × level × language; **no level loses >5%** (a skewed drop changes curriculum weighting).
7. Arrow-glyph distribution preserved per row (`{→: 4157, ->: 165}` on defect turns).
8. Self-loop share of tool-call turns 78.8% → **100%**; corpus-wide self-loop share 37.1% → ~40–41%, which should land near the 41.6% gold expectation (§4.2) — a strong sanity signal.
9. Retry-arc distribution reported and **explicitly unchanged** (`{1: 3784, 2: 26}`, zero exhaustion arcs) — remediation manufactures no retries.

---

## Part B — Generator redesign

### B1. `src/llm_workflow_agents/data/system_prompt.py`

1. **Fix rule 2's worked example** (`system_prompt.py:52`) — `[STATE: VERIFY_PATIENT → TERMINAL]` → `[STATE: VERIFY_PATIENT → VERIFY_PATIENT]`. As written it demonstrates both defects at once.
2. **Promote `STAY_RULE`** (already correct at `system_prompt.py:25-34`) into `FORMAT_RULES` as rule 2, interpolated from the existing constant so there is one copy of the text.
3. **Rewrite rule 7** from `"If a tool returns an error, attempt recovery before escalating."` to state the retry arc: retry the same call at most N times, each retry annotating `[STATE: X → X]`; after N failures stop retrying and either take the workflow's error path or say plainly the step cannot be completed and hand off — still without advancing on the retry turn. N interpolated from the sample's spec.
4. **Invert `TASK_A_STAY_RULE`** to opt-out (`=0` reproduces the v1 byte-identical prompt), preserving ckpt-500/1770 comparability. Rewrite `tests/unit/test_stay_rule_flag.py` inverted, adding `test_disabled_prompt_is_byte_identical_to_v1_baseline` against a checked-in golden string.

### B2. New validator in the generator repair loop

`generate_workflows.py:1584` — insert at **position 3** of the `or`-chain:

```python
violations = (
    find_tool_placement_violations(allowed, msgs, schema_names)
    or _find_transition_violations(valid_edge_pairs, msgs)
    or find_tool_stay_violations(msgs)                      # NEW
    or find_continuity_violations(msgs, initial_name, terminal_names)
    or find_shape_violations(msgs, initiator)
)
```

The chain short-circuits, so position == feedback priority. After the two *referential* checks (a nonexistent tool or edge cannot be fixed by relabelling). Before continuity, because a stay violation's correct repair *changes* the continuity chain — continuity first would emit derivative "turn N transitions from X but previous ended at Y" messages and send the teacher chasing the symptom. Empirically decisive: v1 has 4,333 stay violations and **0** continuity defects, so the two are independent and the reordering costs nothing.

### B3. `_workflow_script.py::build_workflow_script`

Add `*, tool_turn_semantics: bool = False, retry_budget: int = 1`. New per-language template keys, emitted only for tool-bearing states:

- `tool_turn_note` — "the turn that issues the `<tool_call>` stays in `[{name}]`".
- `primary_branch_tool` replacing `primary_branch` — `"- On success: proceed to [{to}] — on a LATER turn, after the tool result has come back"`. This is the exact line review §5.3 identifies as the instruction the model was correctly following into the defect.
- `retry_note` — `"- On tool error: stay in [{name}] and retry at most {n} time(s); after that, {fallback}"`.

**Task C coupling — do not miss.** `_playbook_render.py:240` calls `build_workflow_script`, and `_workflow_script.py` is a declared dep of `task_c_pairs_generate`. Hence `tool_turn_semantics` **defaults to `False`**; both Task A call sites (`generate_workflows._graph_to_script`, `system_prompt.build_enriched_system_prompt`) pass `True`. Add `tests/unit/test_playbook_render.py::test_state_script_unchanged_by_tool_turn_semantics_default`, then `dvc commit task_c_pairs_generate` rather than re-running the teacher-API stage.

### B4. Retry-then-fallback (D4)

`ComplexitySpec` (`config/schema.py:197-222`) gains:

```python
retry_budget: int = 1                                              # attempts of the SAME tool, inclusive
retry_exhaustion: Literal["none","error_path","handoff_in_state"] = "none"
```

L1 `(1,"none")`, L2 `(1,"none")`, L3 `(2,"error_path")`, L4 `(2,"error_path")`, L5 `(3,"error_path")`. `select_subgraph` resolves `error_path` → `handoff_in_state` at sample time when the selected subgraph has no `tool_error` arc out of the failing state — the common case, since `include_recovery` already requires the destination to be pre-selected.

`handoff_in_state`: after N failures the assistant stays in `X` (`[STATE: X → X]`), states plainly that the step cannot be completed and it will hand off, then the workflow continues along the spine on a later turn. **No registry change, no new states, no `validate_domain` edit, no graph invalidation** — and behaviourally correct: an orchestrator that cannot complete a step should not invent a transition.

Teach the same arc to the placeholder generator (`generate_workflows.py:990-1018`), which is the reference shape and the offline test path. **Determinism:** every new draw must sit inside the per-sample `random.Random(child_seed)` scope or `test_data_generation.py::test_concurrent_output_matches_serial` breaks. Add `test_retry_arc_is_deterministic_across_max_workers`.

### B5. `scripts/generate_sft_until_target.py` and `scripts/generate_sft_data.sh`

New flags on both: `--retry-budget N` (default: per-level from `COMPLEXITY_SPECS`), `--retry-exhaustion {auto,error_path,handoff_in_state,none}` (default `auto`), `--require-tool-stay/--no-require-tool-stay` (default on; the off switch regenerates v1-comparable data).

**Qualification bar — do not re-implement the check.** Once B6 lands, `profile_task_a` + `defective_conversation_ids` already remove stay-violating rows at step 3 of `generate_leg`. Add observability only: derive `stay_dropped` by counting defect strings containing `issues a <tool_call> but annotates an advancing transition`, surface it in the per-iteration print line and in the leg stats / `loop_stats_*.json` manifest. One check, one source of truth, full visibility. Thread the new params through `generate_leg(...)` → `generate_workflow_dataset(...)`.

`generate_sft_data.sh` keeps its fixed-curriculum contract (it is the `task_a_sft_generate` DVC stage) but imports `CURRICULUM` from `generate_sft_until_target.py` instead of redeclaring it in the `declare -A` block, and passes the new flags into all three inline `python3 -c` legs.

The **D3 retry slice** (500–800 convs, L3–L5, all three language legs) is generated with `generate_sft_until_target.py --levels L3,L4,L5 --retry-exhaustion auto` and merged into v2 via `scripts/concat_task_a.py`.

### B6. `quality_profiler.py` + `data_validator.py` hard defect

In `profile_task_a`'s per-sample loop, right after the state-sequence equality block (`quality_profiler.py:236`):

```python
for v in find_tool_stay_violations(msgs):
    rep.defects.append(f"{cid}: {v}")     # the f"{cid}: ..." contract defective_conversation_ids parses
```

Plus a distribution entry `"tool_turn_state": {"self_loop", "advancing", "pct_conformant"}`. Mirror the check in `data_validator._validate_workflow_sample` next to the continuity block so both surfaces agree.

Also update `.claude/agents/dataset-verifier.md`, whose step 2 currently says *"Self-loops … are a legitimate generator convention and are not defects — a high self-loop share is expected, not a finding."* Replace: tool-call turns **must** self-loop, `tool_turn_state.pct_conformant` must read 100.0, and a corpus-wide self-loop share materially below ~40% is itself a finding.

**Intended consequence:** `profile_task_a` on v1 (`task_a`, `task_a_cleaned`) will now report 4,333 hard defects, and fixtures in `tests/unit/test_data_generation.py` / `test_data_validator.py` that encode the old convention will fail. Updating them *is* part of the change. `task_a_sft_clean` does not invoke the profiler, so DVC is unaffected.

---

## Model routing (per `.claude/skills/model-routing`)

No Fable item is proposed — the ambiguous design work is resolved by this plan and the measurements behind it. (An independent adversarial review of *this plan* would be the one legitimate Fable ask, and needs explicit confirmation first.)

| Package | Model | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `state_convention.py`, `state_convention_repair.py` + tests | **Opus 4.8** | Crosses 5 enforcement surfaces; silent corpus corruption is the documented failure class; glyph preservation, GT lockstep, split shape legality, the 574-row consecutive-assistant trap, 9 duplicate cids. |
| `build_remediation_ledger.py` (agent driver) | **Opus 4.8** | Concurrency, atomic resumability, subprocess failure modes, and a trust boundary where untrusted LLM output enters a training corpus. |
| `corpus-remediator.md` + playbook | **Opus 4.8** | Judgment-dense; the failure mode (subtly bad Thai/code-switch prose) is not test-catchable. |
| Prompt edits (`FORMAT_RULES`, `STAY_RULE`, `_TEACHER_SYSTEM_PROMPT`, flag-test rewrite) | **Opus 4.8** | Small diff, outsized leverage — baked into every row, gates checkpoint comparability. |
| `ComplexitySpec` retry fields + `select_subgraph` + placeholder arc | **Opus 4.8** | Touches the deterministic-seeding contract and the subgraph selector. |
| `remediate_task_a_states.py` CLI | **Sonnet 5** | Argparse + I/O + reporting over an existing library. |
| `_workflow_script.py` templates + Thai strings + Task C byte-identity test | **Sonnet 5** | Mechanical template work against a specified contract. |
| `_find_violations` insertion, profiler/validator defect, fixture updates | **Sonnet 5** | Three small specified edits; tests catch regressions. |
| Generation script flags + manifest | **Sonnet 5** | Pattern-following plumbing. |
| `dvc.yaml` + lineage/tagging + versioning doc | **Sonnet 5**, human-reviewed | Small but a wrong dep silently trains the wrong lineage. |

---

## Execution order

0. Write the design spec to `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-task-a-tool-stay-convention-design.md` and the implementation plan to `docs/superpowers/plans/`; commit. Branch off `main` (do not commit to `main` directly).
1. `state_convention.py` + `state_convention_repair.py` + tests. **Measure `pullback_fuse` yield in the first hour** — it only shrinks the agent budget.
2. `remediate_task_a_states.py`; run `triage`; confirm the bucket table reproduces.
3. Prompt edits (B1), `_workflow_script.py` (B3), validator wiring (B2/B6) in parallel.
4. `build_remediation_ledger.py`, then `corpus-remediator.md` + playbook.
5. Smoke the agent pass at `--limit 20`; **hand-read all 20 accepted entries**; then the full ledger run.
6. Retry semantics (B4), generation-script flags (B5), D3 retry slice.
7. `dvc.yaml` edits, `dvc repro`, `dvc push`, tag `task-a-sft-v2`.
8. Retrain Cat A SFT on v2; re-audit.

## Verification

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate && python scripts/remediate_task_a_states.py verify \
  --input-dir data/output/sft/task_a_remediated --strict

source .venv/bin/activate && for f in data/output/sft/task_a_remediated/*.jsonl; do
  python -m llm_workflow_agents.data.quality_profiler "$f" | head -5; done

source .venv/bin/activate && python scripts/remediate_task_a_states.py diff \
  --before data/output/sft/task_a --after data/output/sft/task_a_remediated

source .venv/bin/activate && pytest tests/unit -k \
  "state_convention or remediation or clean_task_a or quality_profiler or stay_rule or playbook_render"

.venv-train/bin/dvc repro task_a_sft_remediate task_a_sft_clean task_a_sft_splits task_a_grpo
.venv-train/bin/dvc status
```

Then close the loop on the actual objective with `scripts/analyze_selfloop_habit.py` and `scripts/analyze_composite_decomposition.py` against the retrained checkpoint.

**Pre-registered success criterion** (so a null result is legible): self-loop *emission* rate ≥30% (from 6.4%) and per-turn-fair composite ≥0.75 (from 0.6579, bar 0.80).

## Risk register

| # | Risk | Sev | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Prose/label drift on requeued turns — a turn announces destination Z but is labelled `X→Y`. 258 convs at 1 turn, 82 at ≥2. | High | `RepairPlan.drift_turns` recorded per row; sample 30 drifted rows across languages for human read before accepting; route drift ≥2 to `drop` and backfill if it reads badly. |
| R2 | 5,549 lines but only **5,540 unique `conversation_id`s** (9 duplicates) — any cid-keyed pipeline silently merges rows. | High | Key every artifact `(file_stem, line_index)`; assert `len(records) == line count`; `test_duplicate_conversation_ids_are_not_merged`. |
| R3 | Agent authors plausible-but-wrong text (wrong register, claims work not done). | Med | 3-layer gate incl. Thai-script check; reject→drop, never retry-blind; mandatory hand-read of the first 20; `rationale` on every entry. |
| R4 | Ledger drifts from the corpus after a regen. | Med | `insert_id` embeds `(file_stem, line_index)`; `apply` re-derives the plan and rejects entries whose `required_marker`/context hash no longer matches; ledger carries `schema_version` + source dir DVC hash. |
| R5 | Dropping rows skews curriculum (residual L1 5 / L2 220 / L3 287 / L4 255 / L5 163). | Med | Gate 6 (no level >5% loss); backfill per level/language from the fixed generator before splitting. |
| R6 | `_workflow_script.py` edit invalidates the teacher-API stage `task_c_pairs_generate`. | Med | `tool_turn_semantics=False` default + byte-identity test, then `dvc commit`. |
| R7 | `FORMAT_RULES` change breaks ckpt-500/1770 comparability. | Med | `TASK_A_STAY_RULE=0` opt-out + golden-string byte-identity test. |
| R8 | Generator determinism broken by the retry arc. | Med | All draws inside `random.Random(child_seed)`; `test_retry_arc_is_deterministic_across_max_workers`. |
| R9 | Working dir silently serving the wrong lineage — **has happened twice** (review §1, §6.6). | High | After `dvc repro`, recompute and compare the dir hash against `dvc.lock`; `dvc push` before tagging; record the hash in the tag annotation. |
| R10 | Corpus fixed but policy not retrained → no measured improvement. | High | Retrain + re-audit are part of this work item, with the pre-registered criterion above. |
| R11 | `.bak` / `.corruption-report.json` files live inside the DVC-tracked input dir. | Low | Glob `*.jsonl` only; do not reproduce them into the new out. |

Yes — three things, one of which needs your call.

**Code work: done.** Tasks 1–13 all complete and committed (30 commits on `task-a-tool-stay-convention`), each reviewed with fix rounds. The final whole-branch review came back **ready-with-caveats** and independently re-verified the triage census, deterministic apply, `verify --strict`, profiler defect counts, tool-attribution preservation, and the full pipeline trace. 1,336 tests pass.

**Left:**

1. **One must-fix decision (blocking, needs you)** — detail below.
2. **Plan Task 14 — the ledger authoring run.** `claude -p` over 1,465 conversations / 3,902 inserts. Real API spend, ~$8–13, 1.5–3 h. Gated on your go-ahead; the mandatory `--limit 20` smoke + hand-read comes first.
3. **Plan Task 15 — DVC + retrain.** `dvc repro task_a_sft_remediate … `, `dvc push`, tag `task-a-sft-v2`, plus the D3 retry slice (needs teacher API keys), then the Cat A SFT retrain and re-audit against the pre-registered criterion.

**Deferred, not blocking:** `PYTHONHASHSEED`-dependent nondeterminism in `select_subgraph` — confirmed pre-existing, not introduced here, worth its own ticket. Plus a handful of documented low-severity minors in the ledger.

---

**The blocking decision.** Decision D4 set `retry_budget=1` for L1/L2, which renders the prompt rule as *"do NOT retry it."* But the existing corpus already contains same-tool retries after tool errors at those levels — the reviewer measured **200 of 1,251** retained L1 conversations and **783 of 1,305** L2. So post-remediation an L1/L2 v2 row would pair a don't-retry instruction with data that demonstrates a retry: exactly the train-time contradiction this whole branch exists to remove.

questions.question: L1/L2 currently get retry_budget=1 per decision D4, but the corpus data at those levels already retries (200/1,251 L1, 783/1,305 L2). How should the mismatch be resolved?

options.label: Raise L1/L2 budget to 2 (Recommended)
options.description: One-line change to COMPLEXITY_SPECS: L1/L2 become (2, "error_path"). Prompt then matches the data that's already there; nothing gets stripped. Arguably more correct — complexity level describes graph shape, not whether a failed call may be retried. Reverses D4.

options.label: Strip L1/L2 retries in remediation
options.description: Keep budget=1 and make the data conform: collapse repeated same-tool calls after an error at L1/L2. Preserves D4's intent literally, but is new repair logic on ~983 conversations, needs its own tests + review round, and discards real error-recovery signal.

options.label: Keep as-is, document it
options.description: Ship with the contradiction on L1/L2, recorded as a known limitation. Cheapest now, but it reintroduces the exact prompt-vs-data conflict this branch was built to eliminate, on ~2,556 conversations.

def _is_never_text(char: str) -> bool:
    """True for a character that is never legitimate corpus text.

    Category-based, not a codepoint list: see `_NEVER_TEXT_CATEGORIES`.
    """
    return (
        char not in _TEXT_CONTROL_CHARS
        and unicodedata.category(char) in _NEVER_TEXT_CATEGORIES
    )


def _strip_never_text(text: str) -> str:
    """Drop every control / format / private-use / surrogate / unassigned char."""
    return "".join(ch for ch in text if not _is_never_text(ch))


def _is_meaningful(char: str) -> bool:
    """True if `char` is a letter or digit of a script this corpus is written in.

    The positive half of the content rule. A character has to earn its place:
    it must be a letter (`L*`) or a number (`N*`) AND belong to Latin, Thai or
    the plain digits. Everything else -- punctuation, whitespace, symbols,
    combining marks, and every invisible codepoint in Unicode whether or not
    anyone enumerated it -- contributes nothing.

    This is what closes the Default_Ignorable class the stdlib cannot name.
    U+3164 HANGUL FILLER is a letter, so `category()` alone would admit it; it
    is not a Latin or Thai letter, so it is not meaningful here.
    """
    if unicodedata.category(char)[0] not in ("L", "N"):
        return False
    return unicodedata.name(char, "").split(" ", 1)[0] in _MEANINGFUL_SCRIPTS


def _meaningful_len(text: str) -> int:
    """How many meaningful characters `text` CONTAINS.

    Each SOURCE character is folded with NFKC on its own and contributes at most
    1. Folding is what lets fullwidth Latin (U+FF28 and friends) and superscript
    digits count normally rather than being punished for their encoding; the cap
    is what stops a compatibility character from *multiplying*. NFKC expands some
    single codepoints into several meaningful ones -- U+33AF SQUARE RAD OVER S
    SQUARED folds to "rad/s2", five -- so folding the whole string first let two
    codepoints of visible garbage clear a ten-character floor.

    The cap also slightly under-counts genuine ligatures (U+FB01 "ﬁ" scores 1,
    not 2). That is the right trade: one source glyph is one unit of content, and
    the ligature would have to make up the whole floor to matter. Measured on all
    132,975 corpus turns, capping changes the count of exactly 0 of them.
    """
    return sum(
        1
        for ch in text
        if any(_is_meaningful(c) for c in unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", ch))
    )

=== design 44-52 ===
## Decisions (user-confirmed)

- **D1 (the 930 authoring cases):** a `claude -p` agent authors the missing prose into a reviewable decision ledger; a deterministic 3-layer gate accepts or drops each entry. Rejected alternatives: drop outright (loses 16.8%, skews curriculum) or drop-and-backfill from the generator (cleaner provenance but needs a partial teacher-API regen).
- **D2/D5 (prompt policy):** fix the wrong worked example in `FORMAT_RULES` rule 2, promote the existing (but currently opt-in) `STAY_RULE` to default-on via an inverted `TASK_A_STAY_RULE=0` opt-out (preserves ckpt-500/1770 byte-identical comparability), and rebuild system prompts on v2 rows so the corpus states the rule it now demonstrates.
- **D3 (retry-arc synthesis):** do **not** retrofit retry-exhaustion into v1 rows — there is nothing there to repair. Teach the fixed generator the arc and generate a dedicated 500–800-conversation slice (L3–L5, all language legs) merged into v2.
- **D4 (fallback target):** per-level retry budget (`ComplexitySpec.retry_budget`) with an in-state "handoff" behavior when the graph has no `tool_error` edge, rather than adding a shared `HANDOFF` state to `domain_registry.py`. Avoids invalidating all 18 canonical graphs, Task C graph-pair targets, and `task_a_benchmark`. **Final per-level values: L1–L4 = budget 2 / `error_path`, L5 = budget 3 / `error_path`.**
  - *Superseded sub-decision (final review wave, 2026-08-03):* D4 originally set L1/L2 to budget 1 / `"none"`, which renders the "do NOT retry it" form of the rule. The final whole-branch review measured that the existing corpus already retries at those levels — 200 of 1,251 retained L1 conversations and 783 of 1,305 L2 — so a budget-1 prompt would have shipped paired with data that demonstrates a retry. L1/L2 were raised to 2 / `error_path` to match L3/L4: complexity level describes graph *shape*, not whether a failed call may be retried.

## Core algorithm: whole-trajectory requeue

file.content:
## 5. Drift

`RepairPlan.drift_turns` marks prose turns whose destination changed because the
trajectory was re-derived rather than relabelled in place. It holds 1-based
*assistant-turn* ordinals, not message indices — it is a human-review pointer, not an
addressing handle.

**Read this before designing an audit around it: `drift_turns` turned out to be
low-signal.** Measured on the current corpus:

| Move | conversations | with non-empty `drift_turns` |
|---|---:|---:|
| `relabel` | 608 | **608 (100%)** |
| `insert_handoff_turn` | 866 | 666 |
| `append_closing_pair` | 599 | 599 |
| **total** | 2,073 | **1,873** |

It fires on **every single `relabel` plan**, because the queue-draining turn *always*
has a changed `from` — that is the mechanism, not an anomaly. An audit protocol phrased
as "read every conversation with non-empty `drift_turns`" therefore degenerates into
"read the entire repaired corpus," which is not a usable gate. Do not write one.

### The audit protocol that is actually worth running

Sample-based, ~30 conversations, roughly 45 minutes:

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate && python3 - <<'PY'
import json, random, collections
R = json.load(open("data/interim/task_a_state_triage/report.json"))
pool = [r for r in R["records"] if r["drift_turns"]]
random.seed(20260802)
buckets = collections.defaultdict(list)
for r in pool:
    buckets[(r["language"], r["move"])].append(r)
picked = []
for k in sorted(buckets):
    random.shuffle(buckets[k])
    picked += buckets[k][:4]          # 3 langs x 3 moves x 4 = up to 36
for r in picked:
    print(r["key"], r["conversation_id"], r["language"], r["move"],
          "drift_turns:", r["drift_turns"])
PY
```

Then read each one before/after with the dump script from §8 step 1b, and judge one
question only:

> **Does the prose of each drifted turn still make sense at its new destination?**

Concretely, for each flagged turn: it now claims to arrive somewhere different than it
originally did. Does its text still describe *that* arrival? §3.1's message 20 is the
common, benign shape — a turn that reports a tool result and moves on reads correctly
at either destination, because the prose describes the *result*, not the *state*. The
failure shape to hunt for is a turn whose prose names the destination explicitly
("Let's move on to scheduling your appointment") while the requeue has re-pointed it
somewhere else.

Stratify across all three language legs — the drift pool is 1,873 rows and the
language mix of the authoring queue is 28% code_switch / 28% th / 23% en, so an
English-only sample is not representative.

**Gate:** if more than ~3 of 30 read badly, stop and tighten `plan_repair` (Tasks 2/3)
rather than proceeding to §8 step 4. This is a quality gate, not a formality — the
authoring pass costs real money and its output is only as good as the trajectory it
is authored into.

---

## 6. Ledger contract and the three gate layers

content.text: #23 looks wrong — but that's my dump script, not the repair: `insert_handoff_turn` inserts messages, so aligning before/after by turn *ordinal* is invalid. Fixing the harness and redoing the 12 insert-move samples:

input.command:
source .venv/bin/activate && cat > /tmp/claude-1000/-workspaces-ai-agent-llms/a7991fc5-bb0e-46a5-a8a2-79c243bdffcf/scratchpad/drift_dump2.py <<'PY'
import json, re, sys, collections
sys.path.insert(0, "src")
from llm_workflow_agents.data.state_convention_repair import plan_repair, apply_plan

SR = re.compile(r"\[STATE:\s*([^\]\->→]+?)\s*(?:->|→)\s*([^\]]+?)\s*\]")
sample = json.load(open("/tmp/claude-1000/-workspaces-ai-agent-llms/a7991fc5-bb0e-46a5-a8a2-79c243bdffcf/scratchpad/drift_sample.json"))
by_file = collections.defaultdict(list)
for stem, line in sample:
    by_file[stem].append(line)
only_move = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else None

def a_turns(msgs):
    r = []
    for m in msgs:
        if m.get("role") != "assistant":
            continue
        c = m.get("content") or ""
        mt = SR.search(c)
        r.append({"f": mt.group(1) if mt else "?", "t": mt.group(2) if mt else "?",
                  "tool": "<tool_call>" in c,
                  "prose": SR.sub("", c).strip().replace("\n", " ")})
    return r

lo, hi = int(sys.argv[1]), int(sys.argv[2])
n = 0
for stem in sorted(by_file):
    with open(f"data/output/sft/task_a/{stem}.jsonl", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for i, ln in enumerate(fh):
            if i not in set(by_file[stem]):
                continue
            rec = json.loads(ln); n += 1
            if not (lo <= n <= hi):
                continue
            plan = plan_repair(rec)
            if only_move and plan.move != only_move:
                continue
            for k, ins in enumerate(plan.inserts):
                ins.insert_id = f"{stem}:{i}:{k}"
            ledger = {ins.insert_id: {"content": (ins.required_marker + "\n<<AUTHORED>>")
                                      if ins.required_marker else "<<AUTHORED ACK>>"}
                      for ins in plan.inserts}
            out = apply_plan(rec, plan, ledger_entries=ledger or None)
            print(f"\n{'='*100}\n#{n} {rec['conversation_id']} {rec.get('language')} "
                  f"{plan.move} drift={plan.drift_turns}")
            if out is None:
                print("  apply_plan -> None"); continue
            B, A = a_turns(rec["messages"]), a_turns(out["messages"])
            # align by prose identity: authored inserts have no counterpart in B
            bi = 0
            pairs = []   # (before_ordinal or None, after_ordinal, b, a)
            for ai, a in enumerate(A, 1):
                if bi < len(B) and B[bi]["prose"] == a["prose"]:
                    pairs.append((bi + 1, ai, B[bi], a)); bi += 1
                else:
                    pairs.append((None, ai, None, a))
            assert bi == len(B), f"alignment failed {bi}/{len(B)}"
            for bo, ao, b, a in pairs:
                if b is None:
                    print(f"  --- after-turn {ao}: AUTHORED INSERT   [{a['f']} -> {a['t']}]")
                    continue
                if bo not in plan.drift_turns:
                    continue
                print(f"  --- before-turn {bo} (after-turn {ao}) ---")
                print(f"    BEFORE {b['f']} -> {b['t']}{'  +tool' if b['tool'] else ''}")
                print(f"    AFTER  {a['f']} -> {a['t']}{'  +tool' if a['tool'] else ''}"
                      f"{'   <<DEST CHANGED>>' if b['t'] != a['t'] else ''}")
                print(f"    PROSE  {a['prose'][:280]}")

input.old_string:
**Gate:** if more than ~3 of 30 read badly, stop and tighten `plan_repair` (Tasks 2/3)
rather than proceeding to §8 step 4. This is a quality gate, not a formality — the
authoring pass costs real money and its output is only as good as the trajectory it

input.new_string:
**Gate:** if more than ~3 of 30 read badly, stop and tighten `plan_repair` (Tasks 2/3)
rather than proceeding to §8 step 4. This is a quality gate, not a formality — the
authoring pass costs real money and its output is only as good as the trajectory it
is authored into.

> **Align before/after by prose, not by turn ordinal.** `insert_handoff_turn` adds
> messages, so after-turn *n* is not before-turn *n* — an ordinal-aligned dump makes
> correct repairs look like wild mislabels on all 866 insert rows. `apply_plan` never
> edits existing prose, so prose is a stable join key; authored inserts are the
> after-turns with no match in the before-list.

### Audit result (run 2026-08-03, 36 conversations, 3 languages × 3 moves)

**0 of 36 read badly.** The gate passes with a wide margin, and the corpus-wide
measurement below explains why — the failure shape the protocol hunts for is
structurally impossible here, not merely rare.

Over all 1,873 drifted conversations, 5,082 drifted turns:

| Shape | turns | share |
|---|---:|---:|
| `from` changed, destination identical | 2,093 | 41.2% |
| destination changed | 2,989 | 58.8% |
| — of those, new destination == that turn's **own old `from`** | **2,989** | **100.0%** |
| — of those, re-pointed anywhere else | **0** | **0%** |

Every destination change in the corpus is the same move: **the label is pulled back by
exactly one state.** There is no case of a turn being re-pointed to an unrelated
destination, which is precisely the "prose names the destination, requeue sent it
elsewhere" failure §5 was written to catch.

Reading the sample explains the direction. The v1 labels ran consistently *one state
ahead of the prose*: a turn saying "the claim is approved — next I'll process the
payout" was labelled `→ PROCESS_PAYOUT`, when the payout is explicitly the *next* turn's
work. The requeue pulls it back to `→ APPROVE_OR_DENY`, which is what the prose actually
reports completing. Across the sample the repaired label was **more** faithful to the
prose than the original in every destination-change case, not less. Same pattern in all
three languages (`L4_087` th/code_switch insurance chains, `L3_045_6`/`L3_078_6` en
sales, `L5_051_7` th telecom).

**What the audit *did* surface** is not a trajectory bug but an authoring risk, now
fixed in `.claude/agents/corpus-remediator.md`: in **548 of 599** `append_closing_pair`
conversations (91.5%) the last existing assistant turn **already says goodbye**, so the

content.text:
Step 3 drift audit is done. **Gate passes: 0 of 36 read badly.**

**Sample:** 36 conversations stratified 3 languages × 3 moves, drawn from the 1,873-row drift pool with the playbook's seed. Triage census reproduced exactly first (`3476 / 608 / 866 / 599`).

**The corpus-wide measurement is the real result.** Of 5,082 drifted turns:

| Shape | turns | share |
|---|---:|---:|
| `from` changed, destination identical | 2,093 | 41.2% |
| destination changed | 2,989 | 58.8% |
| — new destination == that turn's **own old `from`** | **2,989** | **100.0%** |
| — re-pointed anywhere else | **0** | **0%** |

Every destination change in the entire corpus is the same move — the label pulled back by exactly one state. The failure §5 tells you to hunt for ("prose names the destination, requeue sent it elsewhere") isn't rare here, it's structurally absent.

Reading the sample explains the direction, and it's the opposite of a risk: **the v1 labels ran one state ahead of the prose.** A turn saying *"the claim is approved — next I'll process the payout"* was labelled `→ PROCESS_PAYOUT`, when the payout is explicitly the next turn's work. The requeue pulls it back to `→ APPROVE_OR_DENY`, matching what the prose reports completing. In every destination-change case I read, the repaired label was *more* faithful than the original. Consistent across all three legs.

**One harness bug, mine, worth knowing about:** `insert_handoff_turn` adds messages, so before/after turn ordinals don't correspond. My first dump aligned by ordinal and made correct repairs on all 866 insert rows look like wild mislabels — I nearly filed `L3_031_9` as a defect before catching it. Re-ran joined on prose (which `apply_plan` never edits). Documented in §5 so the next person doesn't lose the same twenty minutes.

**The audit did find one real thing — an authoring risk, not a trajectory bug.** In **548 of 599** `append_closing_pair` conversations (91.5%) the last existing assistant turn *already says goodbye* — "have a wonderful day", `สวัสดีค่ะ`, `ขอให้เดินทางปลอดภัย`. The authored closing pair lands after that farewell, and `corpus-remediator.md` only said "sign off in the register the agent has been using." That would have produced a second full sign-off on roughly 550 rows — about 14% of the paid pass, spent teaching the model to close twice. The agent file now states the measurement and gives good/bad examples in both registers: the ack raises one small thing, the assistant answers in a sentence and stops.

That's exactly what Step 3 is for — catching it here cost nothing; catching it at Step 4's hand-read would have meant re-running part of the paid pass.

Two commits: `5c502dd` (audit result + agent fix) and the earlier `on-unrepairable` doc correction.

Next is **Step 4** — the free `--dry-run` prompt render, then the ~$0.10 smoke run of 18 inserts across 8 conversations for your hand-read. Say go and I'll run both.

source .venv/bin/activate && python3 - <<'PY'
import json, collections
R = json.load(open("data/interim/task_a_state_triage/report.json"))
c = collections.Counter(); examples = []
for rec in R["records"]:
    for ins in rec.get("inserts") or []:
        if ins["role"] != "assistant":
            continue
        m = ins.get("required_marker") or ""
        body = m[m.find(":")+1:].rstrip("]")
        src, _, dst = body.partition("→")
        adv = src.strip() != dst.strip()
        prev = next((w for w in ins["context_window"]
                     if w["index"] == ins["position_after_msg_index"]), None)
        if prev is None:
            c["prev_not_in_window"] += 1; continue
        if prev["role"] != "tool":
            c[f"prev_role={prev['role']}"] += 1; continue
        try:
            p = json.loads(prev["content"])
        except Exception:
            p = None
        err = isinstance(p, dict) and ("error" in p or p.get("status") == "error")
        k = ("advancing" if adv else "self_loop") + ("_after_ERROR" if err else "_after_ok")
        c[k] += 1
        if k == "advancing_after_ERROR" and len(examples) < 5:
            examples.append((ins["insert_id"], rec["language"], m, prev["content"][:80]))
print(json.dumps(dict(c), indent=2))
tot_adv = c["advancing_after_ERROR"] + c["advancing_after_ok"]
print(f"\nadvancing bridges after a tool message: {tot_adv}")
print(f"  of which the tool ERRORED: {c['advancing_after_ERROR']} "
      f"({100*c['advancing_after_ERROR']/max(tot_adv,1):.1f}%)")
for e in examples:
    print("  ", e[0], e[1], e[2], "|", e[3])
PY

Stopping before the smoke run — the dry-run surfaced a blocking defect. Confirmed on the full trace:

**`plan_repair` drains a queued state advance across a tool *error*.**

In `l1_merged_20260629:101` the repaired trajectory reads:

```
[ 6] assistant [VERIFY_IDENTITY → VERIFY_IDENTITY]  <tool_call verify_identity>   ✓ correct
[ 7] tool       {"error": "Service temporarily unavailable"}
[ 8] assistant [VERIFY_IDENTITY → AUTHENTICATE]     <<AUTHORED>>        ← advances after the failure
[ 9] user       <<AUTHORED ACK>>
[10] assistant [AUTHENTICATE → AUTHENTICATE]        <tool_call verify_identity>   ← retries from the next state
[11] tool       {"status": "success"}
```

That is exactly backwards from the convention this branch exists to install. Rule 4 says *on error, stay and retry; advance only on success.* The repair instead advances on the error and then retries the failed call from the state it shouldn't have reached yet.

It's also unsatisfiable as an authoring request. `corpus-remediator.md` correctly forbids narrating success after an error ("Bad: `Great, that worked!` — the tool errored"), but the `required_marker` demands precisely that advance. The agent's only honest options are refuse (→ conversation dropped) or hallucinate a successful verification.

**Scale: 107 of 912 advancing bridges (11.7%)** land immediately after an errored tool result. Same shape in all three languages, concentrated in `verify_identity` / `run_diagnostics` retry pairs.

The right repair is to keep the advance queued when the intervening tool result is an error — the retry turn is legitimately in-state, and the queued advance drains naturally at the first turn *after* a success. In the trace above that's `[12]` ("ระบบผ่านขั้นตอนนี้เรียบร้อยแล้ว" — *we've passed this step*), which is where the prose already says verification succeeded. That conversation then needs **no authored turns at all** — it collapses from `insert_handoff_turn` to a pure `relabel`.

So the fix likely makes the paid pass both more correct and cheaper. I haven't measured how many of the 107 fully collapse versus still needing a bridge.

I did not run the smoke. Two reasons: 107 of the requests are ones I'd be paying to author wrongly, and fixing this changes the triage report — every `insert_id` is positional, so the batch composition and the whole census shift underneath it. Any ledger built now would be invalidated by the fix.

This is a `plan_repair` change in the Task 2/3 core, so it also means re-running triage, re-checking the census against §1, and a spot-check of the drift audit on the changed rows. Want me to take it?

def test_retry_after_tool_error_stays_in_state_and_needs_no_bridge():
    """A stacked tool turn that RETRIES after an error must not advance.

    The convention's rule 4: on a tool error the next turn stays in the same
    state and may retry; the advance happens only after a success. Before this,
    the walk saw a stacked tool turn, inserted a bridge to carry the displaced
    advance, and so authored a turn asserting `A -> B` immediately after
    `{"error": ...}` — teaching exactly the tool-result hallucination the whole
    convention exists to prevent. Measured on the real corpus: 107 of 912
    advancing bridges (11.7%) landed after an errored tool result.

    Correct shape: both tool turns self-loop at A, the advance stays queued,
    and the prose turn after the SUCCESSFUL result drains it. No authored text
    at all — the conversation collapses to a plain relabel.
    """
    msgs = [
        _amsg('[STATE: A → B]\n<tool_call>{"name": "t1", "arguments": {}}</tool_call>'),
        {"role": "tool", "content": '{"error": "Service temporarily unavailable"}',
         "annotations": None},
        _amsg('[STATE: B → B]\n<tool_call>{"name": "t1", "arguments": {}}</tool_call>'),
        {"role": "tool", "content": '{"status": "success"}', "annotations": None},
        _amsg("[STATE: B → B]\nAll set — verified."),
    ]
    rec = _record(msgs, [("A", "B")], terminal=("B",))
    plan = plan_repair(rec)

    assert plan.move == "relabel"
    assert plan.inserts == []
    repaired = apply_plan(rec, plan, ledger_entries=None)
    assert _markers(repaired["messages"]) == [
        "[STATE: A → A]",   # first attempt self-loops
        "[STATE: A → A]",   # the retry stays put; the error did not advance us
        "[STATE: A → B]",   # the advance lands after the SUCCESSFUL result
    ]
    assert find_tool_stay_violations(repaired["messages"]) == []


def test_stacked_tool_turn_after_a_SUCCESSFUL_result_still_bridges():

def _gains_tool_attribution(
    before: dict[str, list[str]], after: dict[str, list[str]]
) -> bool:
    """True if the repair credits any tool to a state it was not called from.

    The tool-attribution invariant, stated as a SUBSET rather than an equality.
    The property that keeps the corpus safe is "the repair never invents a
    call-site": every (state, tool) pair after the repair must already have
    existed before it. Losing a pair is the opposite of dangerous — it means a
    tool stopped being credited to a state it never legitimately ran from.

    Equality was the original wording, and it was one notch too strong for a
    case it had not anticipated. Fixing the retry-after-error bug (see
    ``state_convention_repair._errored``) relabels a retry turn back to the
    state it actually retried from, which correctly *removes* the wrongly
    advanced attribution. Under equality that dropped 100 conversations —
    precisely the rows demonstrating the retry-then-advance behaviour the whole
    convention exists to teach. Measured on the real corpus: of the 102
    conversations whose map changes, 97 only lose pairs (keep them) and 5
    genuinely move a tool from one state to another (still dropped).
    """
    for state, tools in after.items():
        if set(tools) - set(before.get(state, ())):
            return True
    return False

def test_tool_attribution_guard_allows_losing_a_pair_but_never_gaining_one():
    """The invariant is a subset relation, not equality.

    Losing a (state, tool) pair means the repair stopped crediting a tool to a
    state it never legitimately ran from — that is the retry-after-error fix
    working. Gaining one means the repair invented a call-site, which is the
    corpus-corrupting case the guard exists to catch.
    """
    from remediate_task_a_states import _gains_tool_attribution

    before = {"A": ["t1"], "B": ["t1", "t2"]}

    # unchanged
    assert _gains_tool_attribution(before, before) is False
    # narrowed: the retry stops being credited to B
    assert _gains_tool_attribution(before, {"A": ["t1"], "B": ["t2"]}) is False
    # a whole state's attribution disappears
    assert _gains_tool_attribution(before, {"A": ["t1"]}) is False
    # gained: t2 newly credited to A
    assert _gains_tool_attribution(before, {"A": ["t1", "t2"], "B": ["t1", "t2"]}) is True
    # moved: lost from B, gained at a brand-new state
    assert _gains_tool_attribution(before, {"A": ["t1"], "C": ["t2"]}) is True

source .venv/bin/activate && timeout 1800 python3 - <<'PY'
import json, glob, re, sys, collections
sys.path.insert(0, "src")
from llm_workflow_agents.data.state_convention_repair import plan_repair, apply_plan
SR = re.compile(r"\[STATE:\s*([^\]\->→]+?)\s*(?:->|→)\s*([^\]]+?)\s*\]")
def a_turns(msgs):
    out=[]
    for m in msgs:
        if m.get("role")!="assistant": continue
        c=m.get("content") or ""; mt=SR.search(c)
        out.append((mt.group(1) if mt else "?", mt.group(2) if mt else "?", SR.sub("",c).strip()))
    return out
drift_by_move=collections.Counter(); tot_by_move=collections.Counter()
k=collections.Counter()
ins_comp=collections.Counter()
for f in sorted(glob.glob("data/output/sft/task_a/l*_merged_*.jsonl")):
    for line in open(f, encoding="utf-8"):
        if not line.strip(): continue
        rec=json.loads(line); plan=plan_repair(rec)
        tot_by_move[plan.move]+=1
        # insert composition
        n=len(plan.inserts)
        for idx,i in enumerate(plan.inserts):
            if i.role=="user" and plan.move=="append_closing_pair" and idx==n-2: ins_comp["closing_opener"]+=1
            elif i.role=="user": ins_comp["shape_pad_ack"]+=1
            elif plan.move=="append_closing_pair" and idx==n-1: ins_comp["closing_terminal"]+=1
            else: ins_comp["bridge"]+=1
        if not plan.drift_turns: continue
        drift_by_move[plan.move]+=1
        for j,i2 in enumerate(plan.inserts): i2.insert_id=f"x:{j}"
        led={i2.insert_id:{"content":(i2.required_marker+"\nX") if i2.required_marker else "X"} for i2 in plan.inserts}
        out=apply_plan(rec,plan,ledger_entries=led or None)
        if out is None: continue
        B,A=a_turns(rec["messages"]),a_turns(out["messages"])
        bi=0; amap={}
        for a in A:
            if bi<len(B) and B[bi][2]==a[2]: amap[bi+1]=a; bi+=1
        if bi!=len(B): k["align_fail"]+=1; continue
        for t in plan.drift_turns:
            b,a=(B[t-1] if t-1<len(B) else None), amap.get(t)
            if not b or not a: continue
            k["total"]+=1
            if b[1]==a[1]: k["from_only"]+=1
            elif a[1]==b[0]: k["pulled_back"]+=1
            else: k["other"]+=1
print("drift convs by move:", dict(drift_by_move), "| totals:", dict(tot_by_move))
print("drift turns:", dict(k))
print("insert composition:", dict(ins_comp), "sum:", sum(ins_comp.values()))
PY

## 4. Move ladder and rejected moves

| # | Move | Authored text | Conversations |
|---|---|---|---:|
| 1 | `relabel` — queue drains cleanly (bare and fused tool turns alike) | none | 608 |
| 2 | `pullback_fuse` — move `<tool_call>` onto the preceding `X→X` prose turn | none | **not implemented** |
| 3 | `insert_handoff_turn` — stacked tool turns; insert an assistant bridge (+ ack padding) | 1–13 msgs | 866 |
| 4 | `append_closing_pair` — tail deficit; append `user` ack + terminal `assistant` | 2+ msgs | 599 |
| 5 | `drop` — planner infeasibility, post-gate failure, or agent refusal | — | 0 planner-side |

Move 3 must bridge `cur` to the stacked turn's own `from`-state, **not** a bare
self-loop at `cur` — a self-loop would leave the trajectory exactly as stuck as before.

**`pullback_fuse` was measured and deliberately skipped.** It yielded 14 candidates —
1.2% of what was then a 1,150-conversation insert bucket. Not worth a distinct code
path, so the implemented ladder goes straight from `relabel` to `insert_handoff_turn`.

**Rejected moves:**

- **Splitting a fused turn** (`split_fused_tool_turn`, the original move 2). Keep the
  prose at its claimed destination `X→Y` and move only the `<tool_call>` into a new
  self-loop at `Y→Y`. Measurement killed it: it re-attributes the tool call from `X`
  to `Y` in `infer_state_tools_from_messages`' accounting on ~66% of applicable sites
  (777 of 1,227 shipped split sites, across 360 conversations = 6.5% of the corpus),
  directly violating the "preserve every tool call's `from`-state exactly" rule and
  the "GT-inferred tool→state map unchanged" acceptance gate. Removing it is what
  raised the authoring bucket from 930 to 1,465 conversations, and it drove
  tool-placement violations from 360 conversations to zero. That is the trade, and it
  was accepted.
- **Marker-only inserted turns.** 0 of 64,964 corpus turns are marker-only; adding
  them would teach empty-content turns.

16	## 1. The convention, and why
17	
18	Cat A fine-tuning is stalled on **state-transition accuracy, not tool emission**.
19	`docs/cat_a_state_annotation_convention_review.md` pins the cause: the v1 corpus
20	teaches an unstated and inconsistent convention for which state a tool-calling turn
21	should annotate. Gold expects a self-loop on 41.6% of turns; ckpt-500 emits one on
22	4.8%; accuracy on stay+tool-expected turns is 0.055. Three cheaper fixes were measured
23	and are null — perfect rule application caps composite at 0.7609 (§6.1), prompt-only
24	`STAY_RULE` injection moves self-loop emission 4.84% → 7.87% at Wilcoxon p=0.917
25	(§6.5), and 3.5× epochs gives composite 0.6579 at p=0.513 (§6.6). The corpus itself
26	has to change.
27	
28	**Target convention:**
29	
30	1. A turn emitting `<tool_call>` annotates `[STATE: X → X]` (stay).
31	2. A `role: "tool"` message returns the result.
32	3. On success, the *next* assistant turn advances: `[STATE: X → Y]`.
33	4. On error, the next turn stays `X → X` and may retry the same tool.
34	5. After N failed attempts, stop retrying and take a fallback path.
